docs.title: ocsf-lake
docs.text: A Go library for storing, validating, and querying OCSF (Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework) events with pluggable storage backends.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• OCSF Event Storage - Store OCSF events with automatic extraction of key fields for indexing
  • Pluggable Backends - SQLite (in-memory or file) and PostgreSQL support via Ent ORM
  • Real Schema Validation - events checked against the compiled OCSF schema (required attributes, types, enums, constraints, UID consistency) embedded in ocsf-schema-go
  • Record Integrity - verify signed events (record_integrity profile): on-demand, full, incremental, sampled, and chain checks; verify or attest at ingest; persisted check reports
  • Type-Safe - generated OCSF structs and constants from ocsf-schema-go, with typed ingest and class-UID decode
  • Flexible Querying - Query by class, category, severity, source, time range, and more
  • CLI - ocsflake: ingest, query, check, seed, sign, verify
  • Test Data - deterministic, schema-valid seeding with signed/tampered/chained mixes

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/lake"
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go/ocsf/events"

    _ "github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    // Create a lake with in-memory SQLite
    l, err := lake.New(ctx, lake.WithSQLiteMemory())
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer l.Close()

    // Ingest an OCSF Authentication event
    event := json.RawMessage(`{
        "class_uid": 3002,
        "category_uid": 3,
        "activity_id": 1,
        "type_uid": 300201,
        "time": 1704067200000,
        "severity_id": 1,
        "message": "User logged in successfully",
        "metadata": {"version": "1.10.0", "product": {"name": "my-idp"}},
        "user": {"name": "john.doe"},
        "dst_endpoint": {"hostname": "auth.example.com"}
    }`)

    if err := l.Ingest(ctx, event); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    // Query authentication events
    stored, err := l.QueryByClassUID(ctx, events.ClassUIDAuthentication)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    fmt.Printf("Found %d authentication events\n", len(stored))
}

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
go get github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake

For SQLite support (requires CGO):

go get github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3

docs.title: What is OCSF?
docs.text:
The Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) is an open-source project that provides an extensible framework for developing schemas and a vendor-agnostic core security schema. OCSF enables security teams to normalize and analyze security data across different tools and vendors.

Key OCSF concepts:

  • Categories - High-level groupings (System Activity, IAM, Network Activity, etc.)
  • Classes - Specific event types within categories (Authentication, DNS Activity, etc.)
  • Activity IDs - Actions performed (Login, Logout, Create, Delete, etc.)
  • Type UIDs - Unique identifier combining class and activity

docs.title: ocsflake CLI
docs.text:
ocsflake wraps the library for pipelines and operations: ingest, query, integrity-check, seed, and standalone sign/verify.

go install github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/cmd/ocsflake@latest

docs.title: Global flags
docs.text: Flag Default Purpose --db ocsf-lake.db SQLite database file --memory false in-memory SQLite (single process) --dsn PostgreSQL connection string (overrides --db) --validation strict schema validation mode: strict, permissive, off --unknown-attributes warn attributes not in the OCSF schema: warn, ignore, error --source default source for ingested events

docs.title: Ingesting and querying
docs.text:
# One JSON event per file, or NDJSON on stdin with no arguments
ocsflake ingest event1.json event2.json
cat events.ndjson | ocsflake ingest

# Optional ingest-time integrity: --integrity monitor|enforce plus trust flags
ocsflake ingest --integrity enforce --cert signer.pem --pin <sha256> events.ndjson

ocsflake get <id> [--payload-only]
ocsflake query --class-uid 3002 --since 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z --limit 50
ocsflake query --integrity-status signature_invalid   # events whose recorded check failed
ocsflake count --severity-id 5

query emits NDJSON (stored envelope, or raw payloads with --payload-only); --since/--until accept RFC 3339 or epoch milliseconds.

docs.title: Integrity checks
docs.text:
All check commands share trust flags — --cert (candidate signer certificate PEM, repeatable), --root (trusted root PEM), --pin (hex SHA-256 cert fingerprint) — plus --allow-unsigned (default true) and --record (persist the report and stamp integrity_status on checked events). They exit non-zero when events fail, so they slot into CI and cron directly.

ocsflake check event <id> --cert cert.pem
ocsflake check all --cert cert.pem --record
ocsflake check incremental --cert cert.pem --record   # resumes last recorded checkpoint
ocsflake check sample --percent 5 --max 1000 --cert cert.pem --record
ocsflake check chain <chain-uid> --cert cert.pem
ocsflake check reports [--kind incremental] [--limit 20]

docs.title: Signing and verifying (no lake required)
docs.text:
# Sign an event under the record_integrity profile; chain via --prev
ocsflake sign --key key.pem --signer-cert cert.pem --chain-uid audit e1.json > s1.json
ocsflake sign --key key.pem --signer-cert cert.pem --chain-uid audit --prev s1.json e2.json > s2.json

# Verify content + signatures + certificate trust, and optionally the chain link
ocsflake verify s2.json --cert cert.pem --pin <sha256> --prev s1.json

docs.title: Seeding test data
docs.text:
ocsflake --db demo.db seed --events 5000 --signed-pct 60 --tamper-pct 2 --chains 3 --seed 42
# writes the ephemeral signing key/cert to --keys-dir (default seed-keys/) and prints the pin

ocsflake --db demo.db check all --cert seed-keys/cert.pem --pin <printed-pin> --record
ocsflake --db demo.db check chain seed-chain-01 --cert seed-keys/cert.pem --pin <printed-pin>

--break-chain corrupts one chain link (for exercising chain_broken detection); --ndjson writes generated events to stdout instead of ingesting. See Seed for the underlying package.

docs.text: Real-world usage examples for ocsf-lake.

docs.title: Ingesting Events from AWS CloudTrail
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "encoding/json"
    "log"

    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/lake"
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go/ocsf/events"

    _ "github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    l, err := lake.New(ctx,
        lake.WithSQLiteFile("cloudtrail-events.db"),
        lake.WithDefaultSource("aws-cloudtrail"),
    )
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer l.Close()

    // CloudTrail event converted to OCSF Authentication format
    event := json.RawMessage(`{
        "class_uid": 3002,
        "class_name": "Authentication",
        "category_uid": 3,
        "activity_id": 1,
        "type_uid": 300201,
        "time": 1704067200000,
        "severity_id": 1,
        "status_id": 1,
        "message": "ConsoleLogin succeeded for user admin@example.com",
        "metadata": {
            "version": "1.3.0",
            "product": {
                "name": "AWS CloudTrail",
                "vendor_name": "Amazon Web Services"
            }
        },
        "user": {"name": "admin@example.com"},
        "dst_endpoint": {"svc_name": "signin.amazonaws.com"},
        "unmapped": {
            "eventSource": "signin.amazonaws.com",
            "eventName": "ConsoleLogin",
            "awsRegion": "us-east-1"
        }
    }`)

    if err := l.Ingest(ctx, event); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    log.Println("Event ingested successfully")
}

docs.title: Finding Failed Authentication Attempts
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "time"

    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/lake"
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go/ocsf/events"

    _ "github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    l, err := lake.New(ctx, lake.WithSQLiteFile("events.db"))
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer l.Close()

    // Query failed authentication events in the last hour
    from := time.Now().Add(-1 * time.Hour).UnixMilli()
    to := time.Now().UnixMilli()

    q := l.QueryBuilder().
        WithClassUID(events.ClassUIDAuthentication).
        WithStatusID(events.StatusIDFailure).
        WithTimeRange(from, to).
        OrderByTime(true).
        WithLimit(100).
        Build()

    events, err := l.Query(ctx, q)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    fmt.Printf("Found %d failed auth events in the last hour\n", len(events))

    for _, e := range events {
        msg := e.Payload["message"]
        fmt.Printf("  - [%s] %v\n",
            time.UnixMilli(e.Time).Format(time.RFC3339),
            msg,
        )
    }
}

docs.title: Security Event Dashboard
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "time"

    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/lake"
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go/ocsf/events"
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/storage"

    _ "github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    l, err := lake.New(ctx, lake.WithSQLiteFile("events.db"))
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer l.Close()

    // Last 24 hours
    from := time.Now().Add(-24 * time.Hour).UnixMilli()
    to := time.Now().UnixMilli()

    // Count by severity
    fmt.Println("Events by Severity (Last 24h)")
    fmt.Println("=============================")

    severities := []struct {
        id   int
        name string
    }{
        {events.SeverityIDCritical, "Critical"},
        {events.SeverityIDHigh, "High"},
        {events.SeverityIDMedium, "Medium"},
        {events.SeverityIDLow, "Low"},
        {events.SeverityIDInformational, "Informational"},
    }

    for _, sev := range severities {
        count, _ := l.Count(ctx, &storage.Query{
            SeverityID: &sev.id,
            TimeFrom:   &from,
            TimeTo:     &to,
        })
        fmt.Printf("  %-15s %d\n", sev.name+":", count)
    }

    // Count by category
    fmt.Println("\nEvents by Category (Last 24h)")
    fmt.Println("==============================")

    categories := []struct {
        id   int
        name string
    }{
        {events.CategoryUIDSystem, "System Activity"},
        {events.CategoryUIDFindings, "Findings"},
        {events.CategoryUIDIAM, "IAM"},
        {events.CategoryUIDNetwork, "Network"},
    }

    for _, cat := range categories {
        count, _ := l.Count(ctx, &storage.Query{
            CategoryUID: &cat.id,
            TimeFrom:    &from,
            TimeTo:      &to,
        })
        fmt.Printf("  %-20s %d\n", cat.name+":", count)
    }
}

docs.title: Batch Ingestion
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "encoding/json"
    "log"
    "time"

    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/lake"
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/ocsf"
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go/ocsf/events"

    _ "github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    l, err := lake.New(ctx, lake.WithSQLiteMemory())
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer l.Close()

    // Create batch of events
    var batch []json.RawMessage
    baseTime := time.Now().UnixMilli()

    for i := 0; i < 1000; i++ {
        event := map[string]any{
            "class_uid":    events.ClassUIDNetworkActivity,
            "category_uid": events.CategoryUIDNetwork,
            "activity_id":  1,
            "type_uid":     ocsf.CalculateTypeUID(events.ClassUIDNetworkActivity, 1),
            "time":         baseTime + int64(i*1000),
            "severity_id":  events.SeverityIDInformational,
        }

        data, _ := json.Marshal(event)
        batch = append(batch, data)
    }

    // Ingest batch
    start := time.Now()
    if err := l.Ingest(ctx, batch...); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    log.Printf("Ingested %d events in %v", len(batch), time.Since(start))
}

docs.title: Event Retention Policy
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "log"
    "time"

    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/lake"

    _ "github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    l, err := lake.New(ctx, lake.WithSQLiteFile("events.db"))
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer l.Close()

    // Delete events older than 90 days
    cutoff := time.Now().Add(-90 * 24 * time.Hour).UnixMilli()

    deleted, err := l.Delete(ctx, l.QueryBuilder().
        WithTimeTo(cutoff).
        Build())

    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    log.Printf("Cleaned up %d events older than 90 days", deleted)
}

docs.title: PostgreSQL Production Setup
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "log"
    "os"

    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/lake"

    _ "github.com/lib/pq"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    connStr := os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL")
    if connStr == "" {
        connStr = "postgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/ocsf?sslmode=disable"
    }

    l, err := lake.New(ctx,
        lake.WithPostgres(connStr),
        lake.WithStrictValidation(),
        lake.WithSchemaVersion("1.3.0"),
    )
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer l.Close()

    log.Println("Connected to PostgreSQL successfully")
}

docs.title: Advanced Queries Using Ent
docs.text:
For complex queries, access the underlying Ent client:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "log"

    "entgo.io/ent/dialect/sql"
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/ent/event"
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/lake"
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go/ocsf/events"
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/storage"

    _ "github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    l, err := lake.New(ctx, lake.WithSQLiteMemory())
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer l.Close()

    // Access Ent client for advanced queries
    entStore := l.Storage().(*storage.EntStorage)
    client := entStore.Client()

    // Complex query: Authentication or Network events, high severity
    events, err := client.Event.Query().
        Where(
            event.Or(
                event.ClassUID(events.ClassUIDAuthentication),
                event.ClassUID(events.ClassUIDNetworkActivity),
            ),
            event.SeverityIDGTE(events.SeverityIDHigh),
        ).
        Order(event.ByTime(sql.OrderDesc())).
        Limit(50).
        All(ctx)

    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    log.Printf("Found %d high-severity auth/network events", len(events))
}

import (
    "context"

docs.title: Ingesting Events
docs.text:
Events are JSON documents following the OCSF schema:

import "encoding/json"

// OCSF Authentication event
event := json.RawMessage(`{
    "class_uid": 3002,
    "category_uid": 3,
    "activity_id": 1,
    "type_uid": 300201,
    "time": 1704067200000,
    "severity_id": 1,
    "status_id": 1,
    "message": "User john.doe logged in successfully",
    "metadata": {
        "version": "1.3.0",
        "product": {
            "name": "auth-service",
            "vendor_name": "My Company"
        }
    },
    "user": {"name": "john.doe"},
    "dst_endpoint": {"hostname": "auth.example.com"}
}`)

err := l.Ingest(ctx, event)
if err != nil {
    log.Printf("Ingest failed: %v", err)
}

docs.title: Required Fields
docs.text:
Events are validated against the compiled OCSF schema from ocsf-schema-go. In the default strict mode, each event class's required attributes and constraints apply (for Authentication: activity_id, category_uid, class_uid, metadata, severity_id, time, type_uid, user, and one of dst_endpoint/service). In permissive mode only the structural minimum is enforced:

Field Type Description class_uid int Event class identifier (must be a known OCSF class)

docs.title: Batch Ingestion
docs.text:
Ingest multiple events at once:

events := []json.RawMessage{event1, event2, event3}
err := l.Ingest(ctx, events...)

docs.text:
// Delete all events older than 30 days

docs.title: Strict Mode (Default)
docs.text:
Rejects events missing required OCSF fields:

    lake.WithSQLiteMemory(),
    lake.WithStrictValidation(),
)

docs.text:
Accepts events with warnings:

    lake.WithSQLiteMemory(),
    lake.WithPermissiveValidation(),

docs.title: Disabled

Skips validation entirely:

    lake.WithSQLiteMemory(),
    lake.WithNoValidation(),

    lake.WithSQLiteFile("/data/ocsf.db"),
    lake.WithStrictValidation(),

docs.title: Integrity
docs.text: The integrity package verifies OCSF record_integrity attestations over stored events, using the cryptographic primitives from ocsf-schema-go/recordintegrity.

docs.title: Package
docs.text:
import (
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/integrity"
    ri "github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go/recordintegrity"
)

docs.title: Policy
docs.text:
policy := integrity.DefaultPolicy() // AllowUnsigned: true
policy.Verify = ri.VerifyOptions{
    Certificates:     signerCerts,          // candidate signer certificates
    PinnedCertSHA256: []string{pin},        // and/or Roots: *x509.CertPool
}
policy.RecordReports = true      // persist every check run
policy.RecordEventStatus = true  // stamp integrity_status on checked events
  • AllowUnsigned: true (default) reports unsigned events as warnings under Report.Unsigned; false counts them as failures.
  • RecordReports builds an audit trail of check runs (queryable via Lake.IntegrityReports) and makes incremental checkpoints resumable.
  • RecordEventStatus stamps integrity_status / integrity_checked_at on each checked event (indexed, so dashboards can query verification state).

docs.title: Check modes
docs.text:
checker := l.IntegrityChecker(policy)

res, err := checker.CheckEvent(ctx, id)          // one-off, on-demand
report, err := checker.CheckAll(ctx)             // full sweep
report, cp, err := checker.CheckIncremental(ctx, checkpoint) // since checkpoint
report, err = checker.CheckSample(ctx, integrity.SamplePolicy{
    Percent: 5, MaxEvents: 1000,                 // % of events, capped per run
})
chainReport, err := checker.CheckChain(ctx, "audit-log-2026-09")

CheckChain resolves chain members by attestation chain_uid, verifies each event, and validates every prev_event link against the resolved predecessor.

docs.title: Resuming incremental checks
docs.text:
cp, err := checker.ResumeIncremental(ctx) // checkpoint from last persisted run
report, next, err := checker.CheckIncremental(ctx, cp)

docs.title: Periodic runners
docs.text:
go checker.RunPeriodicIncremental(ctx, time.Hour, start, onReport)
go checker.RunPeriodicSample(ctx, 24*time.Hour,
    integrity.SamplePolicy{Percent: 5, MaxEvents: 500}, onReport)

A monthly budget of N sampled events at a daily cadence is MaxEvents: N/30.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
type Report struct {
    StartedAt, FinishedAt time.Time
    Checked, Verified, Unsigned, Failed int
    Failures        []EventResult // events whose outcome was failed
    UnsignedEvents  []EventResult // when AllowUnsigned
    RecordingErrors []string      // persistence problems (non-fatal)
}

Per-event statuses come from recordintegrity: verified, unsigned, fingerprint_mismatch, signature_invalid, cert_untrusted, cert_expired, chain_broken, malformed.

docs.title: Integrity at ingest
docs.text: See Lake: lake.WithIngestIntegrity(mode, policy) verifies producer attestations during ingestion (Monitor stamps, Enforce rejects with *lake.IntegrityRejectionError), and lake.WithIngestAttestation makes the lake sign every event it receives, optionally chaining them.

docs.title: Lake API
docs.text: The Lake type is the main facade for storing and querying OCSF events.

docs.title: Package
docs.text: import "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/lake"

docs.title: New
docs.text:
func New(ctx context.Context, opts ...Option) (*Lake, error)

Creates a new Lake with the given options.

Example:

l, err := lake.New(ctx,
    lake.WithSQLiteMemory(),
    lake.WithStrictValidation(),
)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
defer l.Close()

docs.text:

Configures the Lake to use in-memory SQLite. Data is lost when the process exits.

docs.title: WithStrictValidation
docs.text:
func WithStrictValidation() Option

Rejects events with any schema violation (missing required attributes, wrong types, invalid enums, violated constraints, inconsistent UIDs). This is the default mode.

docs.title: WithPermissiveValidation
docs.text:
func WithPermissiveValidation() Option

Rejects only structurally unusable events (malformed JSON, missing or unknown class_uid); other schema violations are tolerated.

docs.title: WithNoValidation
docs.text:
func WithNoValidation() Option

Skips validation entirely.

docs.title: WithSchemaVersion
docs.text:
func WithSchemaVersion(version string) Option

Sets the OCSF schema version recorded on stored events. Defaults to events.SchemaVersion from ocsf-schema-go (the version the bindings were generated from).

docs.title: WithDefaultSource
docs.text:
func WithDefaultSource(source string) Option

Sets the default source for events that don't specify one.

docs.title: WithUnknownAttributes
docs.text:
func WithUnknownAttributes(m validate.UnknownMode) Option

Controls how attributes absent from the OCSF schema are treated during validation: validate.UnknownWarn (default), validate.UnknownIgnore, or validate.UnknownError (strict mode then rejects them).

docs.title: WithRawDataRetention
docs.text:
func WithRawDataRetention() Option

Stores each event's original JSON bytes as received (before any lake attestation) in StoredEvent.RawData, preserving forensic evidence at the cost of roughly doubling per-event storage.

docs.title: WithIngestIntegrity
docs.text:
func WithIngestIntegrity(mode IngestIntegrityMode, policy integrity.Policy) Option

Verifies producer record_integrity attestations during ingestion. IngestIntegrityMonitor stamps integrity_status on stored events without rejecting; IngestIntegrityEnforce rejects failing events with *IntegrityRejectionError. See Integrity.

docs.title: WithIngestAttestation
docs.text:
func WithIngestAttestation(a AttestationOptions) Option

Makes the lake sign every ingested event with its own attestation, optionally chaining events tamper-evidently (ChainUID). The chain tail is process-local; persist Lake.ChainTail() and pass it back as InitialChainTail to continue a chain across restarts.

docs.title: OCSF Types
docs.text: The ocsf package holds the storage-side representation of OCSF events. The OCSF standard itself — generated event/object structs, classification constants, enum caption maps, and the class-UID registry — lives in ocsf-schema-go.

docs.title: Package
docs.text:
import (
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/ocsf"          // storage envelope
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go/ocsf/events"  // OCSF standard: events, constants
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go/ocsf/objects" // OCSF standard: objects
)

docs.title: StoredEvent
docs.text:
Represents an OCSF event as stored in the data lake: the original payload plus storage metadata and indexed classification columns.

type StoredEvent struct {
    ID string

    // OCSF classification fields (indexed)
    ClassUID    int
    CategoryUID int
    ActivityID  int
    TypeUID     int
    SeverityID  int
    StatusID    int

    Time       int64     // OCSF event time (epoch ms)
    IngestedAt time.Time // when the lake received it

    Source        string
    SchemaVersion string

    Payload map[string]any // full event payload
    RawData string         // optional raw original event
}

docs.title: Decode
docs.text:
func (e *StoredEvent) Decode() (any, error)

Unmarshals the stored payload into the concrete generated event struct for its class (e.g. *events.Authentication for class_uid 3002), dispatching via the ocsf-schema-go class-UID registry.

stored, _ := l.QueryByClassUID(ctx, events.ClassUIDAuthentication)
decoded, _ := stored[0].Decode()
if auth, ok := decoded.(*events.Authentication); ok {
    fmt.Println(auth.User.Name)
}

docs.title: TimeAsTime
docs.text:
func (e *StoredEvent) TimeAsTime() time.Time

Converts the OCSF epoch millisecond timestamp to time.Time.

Parses a JSON payload into a generic map for storage.

Computes type_uid using the OCSF formula class_uid * 100 + activity_id.

docs.title: Classification constants
docs.text:
Use the generated constants and caption maps from ocsf-schema-go:

events.ClassUIDAuthentication // 3002
events.CategoryUIDIAM         // 3
events.SeverityIDHigh         // 4
events.StatusIDFailure        // 2

events.ClassNames[3002]       // "authentication"
events.ClassCaptions[3002]    // "Authentication"
events.CategoryCaptions[3]    // "Identity & Access Management"
events.SeverityIDCaptions[4]  // "High"

docs.title: Seed
docs.text: The seed package generates realistic, schema-valid OCSF test data for populating a lake — usable from _test.go files or via ocsflake seed.

docs.title: Package
docs.text: import "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/seed"

docs.title: What it generates
docs.text: A weighted mix of 8 event classes — authentication, network_activity, dns_activity, http_activity, file_activity, process_activity, detection_finding, and registry_key_activity (the Windows extension, class_uid 201001) — spread over a time window with weighted severities and realistic value pools. Every template fills its class's required attributes and constraints, so all generated events pass strict schema validation (guaranteed by the package's own tests).

docs.title: Config
docs.text:
res, err := seed.Generate(seed.Config{
    Events:      5000,          // total events (default 1000)
    Span:        30 * 24 * time.Hour,
    Seed:        42,            // content determinism
    SignedPct:   60,            // % signed by the authority
    TamperPct:   2,             // % of signed events corrupted after signing
    Chains:      3,             // tamper-evident chains woven through the data
    ChainLength: 10,
    BreakChain:  false,         // corrupt one link of the last chain
})

Determinism: event content is byte-identical for identical configs; signature bytes are not (ECDSA signing is randomized, and authorities are generated per run).

docs.title: Signing authorities
docs.text:
auth, err := seed.NewAuthority("my-authority") // ephemeral P-256 key + self-signed cert
auth.Pin()                                     // hex SHA-256 cert fingerprint
auth.Policy()                                  // integrity.Policy trusting this authority
keyPath, certPath, err := auth.WritePEM(dir)   // persist for cross-process use (0600)

Authorities are always generated at runtime — key material is never committed to the repository, even for tests.

docs.title: Using the result
docs.text:
// Ground truth per event and in aggregate:
type Event struct{ ID, UID string; JSON []byte; Class string; Signed, Tampered bool; ChainUID string }
res.Signed, res.Tampered, res.Unsigned // counts the integrity checker must reproduce
res.ChainUIDs                          // e.g. ["seed-chain-01", ...]

err = res.Populate(ctx, l)   // ingest into a lake
err = res.NDJSON(os.Stdout)  // or emit NDJSON for `ocsflake ingest`

docs.title: Typical test
docs.text:
res, _ := seed.Generate(seed.Config{Events: 200, SignedPct: 60, TamperPct: 10, Chains: 2, Seed: 11})
l, _ := lake.New(ctx, lake.WithSQLiteMemory())
_ = res.Populate(ctx, l)

report, _ := l.IntegrityChecker(res.Authority.Policy()).CheckAll(ctx)
// report.Verified == res.Signed
// report.Failed   == res.Tampered
// report.Unsigned == res.Unsigned

docs.title: EntStorage Implementation
docs.text: The EntStorage type provides a storage implementation using Ent ORM.

docs.title: Creating Storage Directly
docs.text:
You can create storage instances directly if you need more control:

// In-memory SQLite
store, err := storage.NewSQLiteMemoryStorage(ctx)

// File-based SQLite
store, err := storage.NewSQLiteFileStorage(ctx, "/path/to/db")

// PostgreSQL
store, err := storage.NewPostgresStorage(ctx, connStr)

docs.title: Accessing the Ent Client
docs.text:
For advanced operations:

entStore := l.Storage().(*storage.EntStorage)
client := entStore.Client()

// Use Ent client directly for complex queries
events, err := client.Event.Query().
    Where(event.ClassUIDIn(3002, 3003)).
    Order(event.ByTime(entsql.OrderDesc())).
    All(ctx)

docs.title: Validator
docs.text: The validator package validates OCSF events against the compiled OCSF schema embedded in ocsf-schema-go — no schema files are needed at runtime.

docs.title: Package
docs.text: import "github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/pkg/validator"

docs.title: Validator Interface
docs.text:
type Validator interface {
    // Validate checks an OCSF event against the schema.
    Validate(ctx context.Context, event json.RawMessage) error

    // ValidateClass validates an event against a specific event class schema.
    ValidateClass(ctx context.Context, classUID int, event json.RawMessage) error
}

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
const (
    ModeStrict     Mode = iota // reject any schema violation
    ModePermissive             // reject only structurally unusable events
    ModeDisabled               // skip validation entirely
)
  • ModeStrict rejects events with any schema violation: missing required attributes (profile-aware), wrong attribute types, invalid enum values, violated at_least_one/just_one constraints, and inconsistent class_uid/category_uid/type_uid values.
  • ModePermissive rejects only events the lake cannot index: malformed JSON, missing class_uid, or an unknown event class.
  • ModeDisabled accepts everything.

docs.title: OCSFValidator
docs.text: Schema-backed validator built on validate.New(ocsfdata.MustSchema()) from ocsf-schema-go.

docs.title: NewOCSFValidator
docs.text:
func NewOCSFValidator(mode Mode) *OCSFValidator

Example:

v := validator.NewOCSFValidator(validator.ModeStrict)
if err := v.Validate(ctx, eventJSON); err != nil {
    var result *validator.ValidationResult
    if errors.As(err, &result) {
        for _, e := range result.Errors {
            log.Println(e.Message)
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
func (v *OCSFValidator) Result(event json.RawMessage) *validate.Result

Returns the full validation result (including warnings such as unknown or deprecated attributes), independent of mode. Useful for surfacing diagnostics without failing ingestion.

docs.title: ValidationResult
docs.text:
Returned (as an error) when validation fails:

type ValidationResult struct {
    Valid    bool
    Errors   []ValidationError
    ClassUID int
}

type ValidationError struct {
    Field   string
    Message string
    Path    string
}

docs.title: Release Notes v0.1.0
docs.text: Release Date: June 29, 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This is the initial release of ocsf-lake, a Go library for storing, validating, and querying OCSF (Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework) events with pluggable storage backends.

Events are ingested as raw OCSF JSON. The lake extracts the key classification, time, and source fields into indexed columns, keeps the full payload alongside them, and exposes a query builder and convenience queries over the result.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
go get github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake@v0.1.0

SQLite support requires CGO and the SQLite driver:

go get github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Ent-backed storage on SQLite (in-memory or file) and PostgreSQL
  • Ingest, query, count, and delete through a single Lake facade
  • Strict, permissive, and disabled validation modes
  • Go constants for OCSF categories, classes, severities, and statuses

docs.title: Lake facade (pkg/lake)
docs.text:
• lake.New(ctx, opts...) with WithSQLiteMemory, WithSQLiteFile, and WithPostgres
  • Ingest (single or batch) and IngestWithID
  • Get, Query, Count, Delete, and Close
  • Convenience queries: QueryByClassUID, QueryByCategoryUID, QueryBySeverityID, QueryBySource, and QueryByTimeRange
  • Storage() exposes the underlying backend for advanced use

docs.title: Storage (pkg/storage, ent/)
docs.text:
The Storage interface covers Insert, Get, Query, Count, Delete, and Close, implemented on Ent. Each event is stored with its payload and indexed columns:

  • class_uid, category_uid, activity_id, type_uid
  • severity_id, status_id
  • time and ingested_at
  • source and schema_version
  • optional raw_data

Composite indexes pair class_uid, category_uid, type_uid, and source with time.

docs.title: Query builder
docs.text:
A fluent builder supports filtering by class, category, type, activity, severity, status, and source, plus time range, limit, offset, and ordering by event time or ingestion time.

q := l.QueryBuilder().
    WithCategoryUID(ocsf.CategoryUIDIAMActivity).
    WithSeverityID(ocsf.SeverityIDHigh).
    WithTimeRange(from, to).
    WithLimit(100).
    OrderByTime(true).
    Build()

events, err := l.Query(ctx, q)

docs.title: Validation (pkg/validator)
docs.text:
• Strict (default): rejects events that fail validation
  • Permissive: tolerates non-critical issues
  • Disabled: skips validation

docs.title: OCSF types (pkg/ocsf)
docs.text: Hand-written Go types for the base OCSF event and StoredEvent, along with constants for categories, classes, severities, and statuses.

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
• OCSF types and constants are hand-maintained and cover only a subset of the standard
  • Validation is JSON Schema based and checks a limited set of attributes
  • No record-integrity (signing, verification, or chaining) support
  • No command-line interface

These are addressed in v0.2.0, which moves the OCSF types and validation onto ocsf-schema-go and adds record integrity and the ocsflake CLI.

docs.title: Release Notes v0.2.0
docs.text: Release Date: October 13, 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
v0.2.0 rebuilds ocsf-lake on top of ocsf-schema-go and adds end-to-end record-integrity support and the ocsflake CLI.

The lake is now strictly the datastore/application layer. The OCSF standard itself — generated event and object structs, classification constants, caption maps, the class-UID registry, schema validation, and record_integrity cryptography — is imported from ocsf-schema-go rather than re-implemented here.

docs.title: Library
docs.text: go get github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake@v0.2.0

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
go install github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake/cmd/ocsflake@v0.2.0

Building requires CGO (mattn/go-sqlite3).

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Types, constants, and validation come from ocsf-schema-go v0.1.0
  • Verify-on-ingest and attest-on-ingest, with tamper-evident chaining
  • Five integrity check modes with persisted, resumable reports
  • New ocsflake CLI

docs.title: pkg/ocsf
docs.text:
ocsf.Event, ocsf.ParseEvent, and the classification and metadata constants are removed. Use the generated packages instead:

import (
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go/ocsf/events"
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go/ocsf/objects"
)

ocsf.StoredEvent remains, gaining Decode(), IntegrityStatus, and IntegrityCheckedAt.

docs.title: pkg/validator
docs.text:
The JSON Schema validator, validator.Options, validator.DefaultOptions, and the ErrMissing* sentinel errors are removed. OCSFValidator validates against the embedded compiled schema:

  • ModeStrict rejects any schema violation: missing required attributes, wrong types, invalid enum values, constraint violations, or inconsistent classification UIDs
  • ModePermissive rejects only malformed JSON, a missing class_uid, or an unknown event class
  • ModeDisabled skips validation

Events that previously passed the JSON Schema validator may be rejected under ModeStrict because the semantic validator is stricter.

docs.title: Storage interface
docs.text: Storage gains SetEventIntegrity, SaveIntegrityReport, and ListIntegrityReports. Custom implementations must add them. Ent-backed databases need a migration for the new integrity_status / integrity_checked_at columns and the integrity_checks table.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 is no longer used.

docs.title: Typed ingest and decode
docs.text: IngestTyped accepts generated event structs; StoredEvent.Decode() returns the concrete type for a stored payload via the class-UID registry.

docs.title: Record integrity
docs.text:
• Verify-on-ingest: IngestIntegrityMonitor verifies producer attestations and stamps integrity_status without rejecting; IngestIntegrityEnforce rejects events that fail the policy
  • Attest-on-ingest: the lake signs each event with its own attestation, optionally chaining events via prev_event
  • Checks: on-demand, full, incremental, sample, and chain modes. Unsigned events are warnings under Policy.AllowUnsigned=true (default) and failures otherwise
  • Reports: check runs persist as IntegrityCheck records with incremental checkpoints, and events can be queried by integrity_status

Ingest-time verification runs before the lake's own attestation is added.

docs.title: Ingest options
docs.text:
• Raw-data retention keeps the original bytes as received, before attestation
  • Unknown-attribute policy is configurable through lake options and the CLI
  • Batch ingest errors report the position of the failing event
  • Close is idempotent and safe for concurrent use

docs.title: ocsflake CLI
docs.text:
Command Purpose ingest, get, query, count Load and read events (query supports --integrity-status) check event\|all\|incremental\|sample\|chain\|reports Run and review integrity checks sign, verify Sign and verify event files seed Generate deterministic schema-valid test data

Command data is written to stdout and status text to stderr, so output can be piped.

docs.title: Seed generator (pkg/seed)
docs.text: Deterministic, schema-valid test events in signed, tampered, and chained mixes. Signing authorities are generated at runtime; no key material is committed.

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
• The attest-on-ingest chain tail is process-local; after a restart the chain starts a new segment unless InitialChainTail seeds it
  • metadata.uid and attestation chain_uid are not yet indexed columns, so chain checks scan payloads
  • Batch ingest aborts on the first error rather than returning per-event results

See docs/specs/ROADMAP.md (Phase 5) for planned work.

docs.title: ROADMAP — ocsf-lake
docs.text: Status legend: planned | in_progress | done. Phase status is derived from member RMI statuses. The OCSF standard layer (bindings, validator, record-integrity crypto) is tracked separately in ocsf-schema-go's roadmap.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Core lake (initial scaffold)
docs.text: RMI Title Status RMI-OCSFLAKE-001 Ent storage (SQLite memory/file, PostgreSQL), StoredEvent envelope with indexed classification columns done RMI-OCSFLAKE-002 Lake facade: ingest, query builder, convenience queries, count, delete done RMI-OCSFLAKE-003 Validator interface with strict/permissive/disabled modes done

docs.title: Phase 2 — ocsf-schema-go integration
